header:
Date: 2029-02-14
Time: 15:00 PT / 23:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Ironforge VP Eng), Lina Gomez (Ironforge Cloud Architect), Marcus Yuan (Ironforge SecOps), Anya Kotecha (Ironforge Platform)
summary: Initial network intake for Ironforge evaluation of Redwood Private. Focus on private endpoints, Transit Gateway peering, egress IP requirements for finance/regulatory workloads, and region restrictions. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private with VPC-onramp; wants clear egress IPs, SOC2 docs, and pilot plan.
topics: Egress IP stability and NAT requirements
Multi-region model hosting and data residency
Latency vs cost tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Maya from Redwood here, with Diego and Priya from our SE team. Quick audio check?
00:08 Ravi Patel: Yep, we can hear you. Thanks. Ravi from Ironforge.
00:12 Maya Chen: Awesome. High level, this is intake for our private/VPC options — just to understand your network layout, egress constraints, and any regulatory region locking. Diego, do you want to kick off what we usually ask?
00:24 Diego Alvarez: Sure. We'll cover where your workloads live today, VPC topology, whether you use Transit Gateway or peering, whether you need a fixed egress IP, and any air-gapped/on-prem segments. Also curious about expected RPS and token volumes for pilot.
00:36 Lina Gomez: Quick context: we run multi-account AWS in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, some on-prem in our DC in Frankfurt. We use TGW heavily and have strict egress IP allowlists for partner integrations.
00:47 Priya Nair: Got it. And are you thinking Redwood Hosted with private endpoints, Redwood Dedicated reserved pool, or full Private (customer VPC) deployment?
00:56 Marcus Yuan: We're leaning Private — we need KMS integrated and no traffic crossing public internet for inference. Also, financial compliance wants stable egress IPs per region.
01:05 Diego Alvarez: OK, so KMS/HSM integration and stable egress are two drivers. For Private we can run our control plane in Redwood with your VPC peered, or a customer-managed control plane in VPC for stricter policies.
01:17 Ravi Patel: Can you explain the difference between peering and TGW in your pattern? We've seen both in your docs but want the tradeoffs.
01:25 Diego Alvarez: Yes. VPC peering is 1:1 and simpler — good for small numbers of VPCs. Transit Gateway lets you attach many VPCs and on-prem via VPN or Direct Connect; it centralizes routes. For high-scale multi-account orgs TGW is cleaner. Also TGW makes egress pathing and IP NATing more predictable.
01:44 Lina Gomez: Our TGW already does NAT for egress and we SNAT to a small pool of static IPs. We need Redwood to either accept peering to a dedicated VPC that sits behind our TGW, or accept incoming traffic through a private endpoint in our VPC that then routes to the Redwood nodes.
01:59 Priya Nair: Two common patterns: (A) Redwood creates a private VPC in our infra and we peer it into your TGW, or (B) Redwood exposes PrivateLink-style endpoints so you keep all control. Pattern A often needs route table planning, pattern B needs us to provision interface endpoints in your subnets.
02:18 Marcus Yuan: For compliance we prefer B — PrivateLink endpoints — because it keeps control in our account. But our security team is worried about outbound egress from Redwood-hosted compute back to other AWS services.
02:30 Diego Alvarez: Understood. For pattern B we can host inference in a dedicated subnet in Redwood VPCs and expose an interface endpoint. All traffic stays within the AWS backbone. We also provide an option where the inference nodes are deployed into your VPC (Private deployment), which gives full egress control — you NAT as you like.
02:47 Lina Gomez: If inference nodes are in our VPC, what about scaling and maintenance? We don't want to manage kernels or model loading.
02:54 Diego Alvarez: Redwood Private can be run in a managed tenant mode: we handle runtime and upgrades but the compute sits in your account (customer VPC). You get the operational windowing and we support autoscaling through our operator. There's an onboarding checklist for subnets, SG, IAM role for cross-account operator, and SSM access patterns.
03:12 Ravi Patel: Important: our external partners expect calls from a set of egress IPs per region — can Redwood guarantee a small static set?
03:21 Priya Nair: For Dedicated pools we can reserve NAT gateways and advertise a small egress set. For Hosted private endpoints there's more variability, but we do support BYO-eips for Dedicated and Private so you can NAT behind your TGW IP set.
03:34 Marcus Yuan: Also, data residency: inference must not leave eu-west-1 for EU customer data. If we send prompts from Frankfurt, model hosting must be in EU.
03:42 Diego Alvarez: We have model variants in regional pools; we can pin a model to eu-west-1. For fallback we can configure a policy to disallow cross-region failover for those pinning rules. That may add capacity constraints but ensures residency.
03:56 Lina Gomez: Latency: we need sub-80ms tail for token generation for some interactive flows. How much does regional hosting vs cross-region add?
04:05 Diego Alvarez: If you host in the same AZ/region, you'll see best latency — we publish per-model perf profiles. Cross-region routing adds additional network RTTs; also, quantization and batching affect tail lat. We recommend Dedicated for stricter SLOs because you get predictable GPU pools.
04:21 Ravi Patel: Pricing question: what's the delta between Dedicated and Private?
04:25 Maya Chen: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool hosted in Redwood infra but dedicated to you — predictable throughput and static egress options. Private (customer VPC) usually has a platform fee plus compute. We'll send a side-by-side pricing sheet, but expectation: Private has higher ops integration cost; Dedicated is often cheaper than full Private for raw $/token at scale.
04:43 Anya Kotecha: We have a small on-prem Hadoop cluster and some inference traffic might originate there, routed through our DC NAT. Will Redwood support hybrid on-prem connectivity?
04:52 Diego Alvarez: Yes — we support VPN and Direct Connect attachments into Redwood TGW or your Transit fabric. In Private mode, since nodes are in your VPC, the traffic is natively in your network.
05:02 Marcus Yuan: Security specifics: do you support SAML SSO for console, RBAC, audit logs to our SIEM, and customer-managed KMS for model artifacts?
05:12 Priya Nair: Yes to SAML and RBAC, audit logs can be forwarded to CloudWatch/CloudTrail and then to your SIEM. Customer-managed KMS is supported for keys; HSMs via partner integrations possible. We'll attach SOC2 / security pack in the follow-up.
05:26 Ravi Patel: For private link we need the interface endpoints subnets to be dedicated and follow our NACL rules. Is that possible?
05:33 Diego Alvarez: Yes, interface endpoints are provisioned in the subnets you choose. We usually ask for two subnets in different AZs, correct route tables, and security group rules allowing the control-plane ENIs to reach the worker nodes.
05:48 Lina Gomez: Any constraints on IP ranges? Our VPCs use 10.1.0.0/16 and several /24s reserved; we need to avoid collisions.
05:56 Priya Nair: We'll provide recommended non-overlapping CIDRs for the deployment. For Private deployments into your VPC, you'll control the worker subnets. For peered setups we recommend an allocation that doesn't conflict with your org.
06:08 Anya Kotecha: Operational question: how are kernel updates and model rollouts handled in Private mode? We need controlled windows and rollback.
06:16 Diego Alvarez: Rollouts are orchestrated through our control plane with canary policies you configure — you can set maintenance windows, automatic rollback on QoE regression, and pin model versions. We integrate with your monitoring hooks so you can trigger failovers.
06:29 Ravi Patel: Does Redwood provide egress IP pooling per account? We need a list for firewall rules.
06:35 Priya Nair: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we can publish stabilized egress IPs. For Hosted public endpoints we cannot promise a stable small list.
06:43 Lina Gomez: There's a vendor that requires TLS client certs for mutual TLS. Can Redwood present client certs from nodes or do we need a proxy?
06:50 Diego Alvarez: Mutual TLS from the inference nodes to external partners is supported but usually customers front that with their NAT/proxy for cert management. We can also support mTLS from nodes if you provide certs and we include them in the deployment during onboarding.
07:03 Maya Chen: Let's walk through a minimal pilot: 1) pilot in eu-west-1, deploy a small Dedicated pool or Private nodes in your VPC, 2) run synthetic throughput and tail-latency tests, 3) validate egress IPs and SOC2 docs, 4) expand to us-east-1. Does that align?
07:18 Ravi Patel: Yes. Questions: how much engineering involvement for Private?
07:22 Diego Alvarez: Typically a small cross-functional window: cloud architect + secops + 2 devs for initial setup, 2-4 weeks for onboarding and network approvals. If you choose Dedicated with PrivateLink, less on-prem effort.
07:33 Marcus Yuan: On auditing — can we get access logs at token-level or just request-level?
07:39 Priya Nair: We log request metadata and can surface per-request token counts and model IDs in audit logs. We avoid logging customer prompt/response content by default unless you opt into content logging for debugging.
07:50 Lina Gomez: Latency verification — can you run a tail-latency bench from our Frankfurt DC?
07:54 Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can schedule synthetic tests from your endpoints and share the raw traces. We'll need a test harness and API keys scoped to pilot.
08:03 Ravi Patel: Any blockers for us from a compliance standpoint? SOC2 is fine; we also need to ensure our EU data doesn't hit US backups. Is that configurable?
08:12 Maya Chen: Yes, you can disable cross-region backups and select region-specific storage. We'll put that in the runbook.
08:20 Anya Kotecha: What about IP blacklisting and CIDR updates — if we change TGW routes, how quickly does Redwood adapt?
08:27 Diego Alvarez: Route changes propagate through the cloud fabric; for PrivateLink there's minimal change. For peering/TGW attachments we recommend a change freeze during maintenance, but Redwood's operator reconciler will adapt within minutes once route tables are updated.
08:40 Maya Chen: Recap and next steps: Diego will share example Transit Gateway config and IP ranges; I'll send SOC2 + security pack; Priya will attach a PrivateLink quickstart. Ironforge to share VPC CIDR, TGW architecture, and preferred pilot region. We'll target the week of Feb 26 for the network workshop.
08:57 Ravi Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
09:01 Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with minutes and the artifacts.
09:05 [call ends]
